summary.oneLiner: The Hi-Tech Gears Limited is an Indian auto-component manufacturer built on technical expertise in precision gears and advanced transmission equipment, with exports at 25.98% of standalone turnover in FY 2025-26.
summary.business: The Company makes precision gears and advanced transmission equipment for the automobile and auto-component industry, selling to domestic customers and to export markets. Management describes a diversified customer base and product portfolio and positions the Company to supply both conventional internal-combustion platforms and emerging electric-mobility platforms. Alongside its standalone Indian operations it reports consolidated performance covering its subsidiaries.

On captive renewable power the Company commissioned a 3.25 MW AC captive solar power plant generating about 7.20 million units a year, operationalised a 2.25 MW AC captive solar plant in April 2024 (about 5.20 million units a year) and commissioned an additional 0.75 MW AC captive solar plant in December 2024 (about 1.70 million units a year), alongside continued use of rooftop solar plants of 400 KW and 250 KW. The Bhiwadi plant is described as a state-of-the-art 'ECOFAC' sustainable green manufacturing plant with a Platinum rating from the Indian Green Building Council, and the Manesar manufacturing unit has also been upgraded to ECOFAC status with an IGBC Platinum award. Stated future plans are development of new products, use of another 100 KW rooftop solar plant, addition of a new furnace with higher capacity and lower energy consumption, projects to optimise motor capacity in machines, reduce forge-shop induction billet heater power and thermally coat furnaces, and exploring the feasibility of off-site captive power generation through a solar or hybrid renewable power plant in Haryana for the Manesar plant.

risks.note: Management flags continuing tensions across Europe, the Middle East and Asia - the Russia-Ukraine war, the America-Iran war and America's trade tariffs - as sources of supply-chain disruption, higher logistics costs and uncertainty in commodity markets and international trade flows. The Chairman adds that the US-Iran conflict pushed Brent crude past $120 per barrel and lifted shipping costs by up to 300% on certain routes.

Steel, alloy steel and other metal-based raw materials are a significant portion of the Company's production cost. Price swings driven by demand-supply imbalances, geopolitical events, inflation, energy costs and trade restrictions can hit operating margins where increases cannot be passed on immediately; mitigation is strategic sourcing, vendor diversification, value engineering and negotiated price revisions with customers.

risks.risk: Shortage of semiconductors and electronic components
risks.note: The industry is exposed to shortages or delayed availability of semiconductors, electronic chips and sensors, which matter more as vehicles get more electronic content; disruption can cause production delays, higher procurement cost and missed customer deliveries. The Chairman notes the global chip shortage has been intensified by the AI investment boom.

risks.risk: Technological disruption and the ICE-to-EV transition
risks.note: Electrification, connectivity, autonomous technology and digital manufacturing are changing customer requirements and product specifications; companies that fall behind risk product obsolescence and market-share loss. The transition also forces simultaneous investment in new technologies and continued support of traditional internal combustion engine platforms, with the pace dependent on charging infrastructure, battery costs, incentives and consumer acceptance.

Global supply chains remain vulnerable to geopolitical conflict, transport bottlenecks, natural disasters, material shortages and trade-policy change, which can delay procurement, raise logistics cost and disrupt production schedules. The Company responds by broadening its supplier base to reduce single-source dependence, strengthening localization and holding optimum inventory of critical materials.

Evolving requirements on emission standards, vehicle safety norms, environmental protection, ESG reporting, labour regulation, product quality and corporate governance raise compliance obligations; failure to comply could bring financial penalties, operational disruption and reputational damage, and future changes may require further spend on product development, testing and certification.

The MD&A opens a dedicated 'Foreign Exchange Risks' sub-heading among its threats and mitigation strategies, but the routed bundle is cut off mid-heading so the Company's own description of the exposure and its mitigation is not available in this text.

The Chairman states that the geopolitical headwinds elevated input costs across energy, petrochemicals, aluminium and freight, and that the Company has been actively managing these pressures through supply chain engagement, energy optimisation and operational discipline. The MD&A adds that volatility in energy prices and transportation costs continues to influence manufacturing and logistics expenses.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Electrification is the key demand driver: rising EV adoption is driving demand for advanced transmission systems, precision-engineered components, lightweight materials and electric drivetrain solutions, which management says positions the Company favourably
- Domestic demand strengthened meaningfully in the second half of FY 2025-26, accelerated by a consumer shift toward premium motorcycles and scooters across both EV and ICE platforms
- North American export revenues softened as the core customer base adopted a wait-and-watch approach on tariff fluctuations and geopolitical uncertainty
- Industry volume backdrop: SIAM-reported total vehicle production up about 11.8% in FY 2025-26, with two-wheelers and three-wheelers leading domestic growth and exports up 24.1%
- China+1 supply-chain diversification and global OEM sourcing from India support export opportunity for Indian component makers
- Higher value addition, increased content per vehicle and greater participation in global supply chains support long-term component-industry growth
- Margin pressure from rising input and labour costs, commodity price volatility and an unsettled geopolitical environment
- Policy support - Make in India, PLI schemes, PM E-DRIVE, National Logistics Policy and the Vehicle Scrappage Policy - underpins the medium-term demand outlook

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strategic focus on optimizing asset utilization, deepening customer relationships, enhancing cost-efficiency, pursuing manufacturing excellence and upholding top-tier product quality
- Lean into electrification: deepen development of advanced technology and EV-specific components while strengthening the core engineering capabilities behind design and manufacturing, with the stated objective of sitting at the technological frontier of the mobility transition rather than at its margins
- A deliberate consolidation phase in the India operations - sharpening operational efficiency through comprehensive machine refurbishment and targeted labour productivity initiatives rather than chasing volume
- Penetrate new markets and expand high-margin revenue streams, leveraging technical expertise in precision gears and advanced transmission equipment
- Strengthen supply-chain resilience through supplier diversification, localization and close collaboration with customers and suppliers
- Continued emphasis on new product development, cost optimization, quality enhancement and capacity utilization
- Return capital to shareholders - a final dividend recommended for FY 2025-26 as an enduring commitment to capital return

- Shortage of semiconductors and electronic components — The industry is exposed to shortages or delayed availability of semiconductors, electronic chips and sensors, which matter more as vehicles get more electronic content; disruption can cause production delays, higher procurement cost and missed customer deliveries. The transition also forces simultaneous investment in new technologies and continued support of traditional internal combustion engine platforms, with the pace dependent on charging infrastructure, battery costs, incentives and consumer acceptance.
- Supply-chain disruption and supplier concentration — Global supply chains remain vulnerable to geopolitical conflict, transport bottlenecks, natural disasters, material shortages and trade-policy change, which can delay procurement, raise logistics cost and disrupt production schedules. The Company responds by broadening its supplier base to reduce single-source dependence, strengthening localization and holding optimum inventory of critical materials.

The MD&A adds that volatility in energy prices and transportation costs continues to influence manufacturing and logistics expenses.
